corrected_draft.title: Trump Orders Detention Pending Immigration Removal Proceedings
corrected_draft.description_short: On January 20, 2025, Trump’s immigration executive order directed detention pending removal proceedings or removal to the extent permitted by law.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Protecting the American People Against Invasion.” The order directed the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that noncitizens apprehended under specified provisions are detained pending further proceedings regarding their removal or removal from the United States, to the extent permitted by law. The text does not establish unlimited or indefinite detention without charge.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed the executive order “Protecting the American People Against Invasion.” The order directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that noncitizens apprehended under specified provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act are detained pending further proceedings regarding their removal from the United States, or removal from the country, to the extent permitted by law. Other sections revoked four earlier immigration-policy orders, established nationwide federal-state homeland-security task forces, and directed agencies to enforce final removal orders. Section 10 also directed DHS to build or use detention facilities and to ensure detention pending removal proceedings or removal, but only to the extent permitted by law. The order does not state that it created unlimited detention without charge. Its date and wording support a narrower description of a federal detention directive under existing immigration law.
